simple.meaning: נֶכֶר (neker) is a Hebrew word meaning “something strange , i.e. unexpected calamity.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: נֶכֶר (H5235) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 31:3, with occurrences in Job, Obadiah.

simple.summary: נֶכֶר (neker) / H5235 is traced through Job 31:3, Obadiah 1:12 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

occurrences.englishText: Is it not calamity to the unrighteous,
But don’t look down on your brother in the day of his disaster, and don’t rejoice over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction. Don’t speak proudly in the day of distress.
